database_and_version: KEGG (GENOME + pathway maps; specific release not logged by the pipeline)
evidence_layer: Bridge: microbial genome-resolved KEGG pool index (descriptive, n=1 pooled/group) -> curated host KEGG pathway (no cross-layer covariance claimed)
host_genes_in_pathway: None of the 6 shortlisted host hub genes. GSEA over the M6 module (both kME and DESeq2-statistic rankings) finds map03320 present in the tested gene-set universe (13 M6 genes overlap the pathway) but NOT significant: NES=1.13 padj=0.61 (kME ranking), NES=-1.19 padj=0.96 (DESeq2 ranking). Reported as tested-and-not-significant, not omitted.
taxa_in_pathway: Top Jumper-side contributors (summed KEGG pool index, butanoate+propanoate+fatty-acid-degradation): Arcticibacterium luteifluviistationis, Klebsiella variicola, Pectobacterium cacticida, Flavobacterium jumunjinense, Pseudoalteromonas phenolica. Top Laggard-side: Cutibacterium acnes (contaminant-flagged, excluded from shortlists but functionally present), Moraxella osloensis, Cupriavidus necator, Exiguobacterium aestuarii, Pseudomonas alkylphenolica.
enrichment_method: Microbial: KEGG GENOME-resolved pool profiling, 3 source pathways bridged by curated literature mapping (butanoate/propanoate metabolism, fatty-acid degradation -> PPAR ligands). Host: clusterProfiler GSEA (KEGG gene sets) over M6, two rankings.
statistic_reported: Rank score = edge_count(3) x |M6 partial_r(WG|sex)|(0.5898) x biological_relevance_factor(1.0) = 1.769. Descriptive microbial pool-index log2 ratios: butanoate -1.36, propanoate -1.54, fatty-acid degradation -1.53 (Laggard-enriched pool index; NOT a statistic -- n=1 pooled/group cannot yield a p-value). Host GSEA padj values above ARE real host-layer statistics (n=20) and are not significant.
statistic_attributable_to: microbial pool index: descriptive only, not attributable to a statistical layer (n=1 pooled/group). Host GSEA padj: host RNA-seq (replicated, n=20 libraries).
mechanism_justification: The top-ranked bridge by this study's own formula, driven by having 3 independent microbial source pathways (more corroborating routes than the other two candidates) rather than by a larger biological-relevance weight. SCFA (butyrate/propionate) are well-established PPAR ligands in mammalian gut-microbiome literature (den Besten et al. 2013); the Laggard-side enrichment of SCFA-pathway genera is directionally consistent with M6's negative correlation with growth, but the GSEA null result means this is a plausible bridge hypothesis, not a demonstrated host-pathway response.

pathway_name: Amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism
database_and_version: KEGG (GENOME + pathway maps; specific release not logged by the pipeline)
evidence_layer: Bridge: microbial genome-resolved KEGG pool index (descriptive, n=1 pooled/group) -> curated host KEGG pathway (no cross-layer covariance claimed)
host_genes_in_pathway: One M6 module member at single-gene resolution: XM_067104953.1, N-acetylgalactosamine kinase (Galk; 49.5% identity to GALK2_RAT), a member of map00520 by orthology -- but this gene is NOT one of the 6 shortlisted top hub genes, and the pathway is NOT among M6's significant GSEA sets (amino sugar metabolism NES/padj not significant on either ranking). This is reported as a single-gene overlap, not a pathway-level result (manuscript section 6.5).
taxa_in_pathway: Top Jumper-side contributors: Klebsiella variicola, Citrobacter koseri, Pectobacterium cacticida, Arcticibacterium luteifluviistationis, Pseudoalteromonas phenolica. Top Laggard-side: Cutibacterium acnes (contaminant-flagged), Moraxella osloensis, Exiguobacterium aestuarii, Cutibacterium namnetense (contaminant-flagged), Mariniblastus fucicola. 6 further Jumper-exclusive Pseudoalteromonas spp. (below the individual taxon ranking cutoff) also contribute chitinolytic KO terms to this pool index.
enrichment_method: Microbial: KEGG GENOME-resolved pool profiling, 1 source pathway (self-mapped). Host: DIAMOND-vs-Swiss-Prot orthology (single-gene) + clusterProfiler GSEA (KEGG gene sets) over M6, two rankings.
statistic_reported: Rank score = edge_count(1) x |M6 partial_r(WG|sex)|(0.5898) x biological_relevance_factor(1.5) = 0.885. Descriptive microbial pool-index log2 ratio: -1.46 (Laggard-enriched pool index; NOT a statistic, n=1 pooled/group). Host GSEA: not significant on either ranking (see host_genes_in_pathway column).
statistic_attributable_to: microbial pool index: descriptive only, not attributable to a statistical layer (n=1 pooled/group). Single-gene orthology hit and GSEA padj: host RNA-seq (replicated, n=20 libraries).
mechanism_justification: Chitin-degrading Jumper-associated taxa (Pseudoalteromonas spp., genome-resolved contributors above) plausibly supply GlcNAc as a growth substrate for exoskeleton synthesis during moulting -- a literature-grounded, biologically specific hypothesis (Raimondi et al. 2023) that is this study's headline microbial mechanism. It is explicitly ranked #2, not #1, because the pathway-level host GSEA test does not support it: the one host-side gene in this pathway (GalNAc kinase, in M6) is a single-gene, not pathway-level, observation, and this is stated rather than allowed to imply a stronger host-side result than the data support.

statistic_reported: Rank score = edge_count(1) x |M6 partial_r(WG|sex)|(0.5898) x biological_relevance_factor(1.5) = 0.885 (tied with rank #2; both driven by the same amino-sugar microbial pool index and the same biological_relevance_factor).
